K1.stone_why: Moderate polygonal faceting on curves gives the display text a clearly hewn, inscribed feel without losing the classical serif base.
K1.carving_why: Facets are applied consistently across letters and digits and read as deliberate cuts; 3/8 and 0/O stay distinct, though some bowls (S, 6) look slightly lumpy at the largest size.
K1.calm_why: Regular weight stays quiet and steady; the bold has presence without shouting.
K1.personality_why: The chiselled facets give a recognisable voice beyond a stock serif.

K2.stone_why: Faceting is fine-grained, so the text reads mostly as a smooth serif with only a faint hewn quality.
K2.carving_why: Cuts are clean and coherent but so subtle they barely register as carving at display size; digits are fully legible.
K2.calm_why: Very calm and composed, with enough weight in the bold to hold presence.
K2.personality_why: Hard to tell from the plain serif except on close inspection; character is understated.

K3.stone_why: A smooth, conventional transitional serif; only its classical capitals hint at inscription.
K3.carving_why: No visible carving; curves are fully smooth.
K3.calm_why: Calm, even and well-balanced with confident bold weights.
K3.personality_why: Handsome but generic book serif with nothing distinctly its own.

K4.stone_why: Visible faceting on bowls and terminals reads as chiselled stone, very close to K1.
K4.carving_why: Coherent, crisp facets across letters and numerals; digits remain easy to separate, with only minor unevenness on S and 6.
K4.calm_why: Steady and grounded; the angularity adds presence without aggression.
K4.personality_why: Distinct hewn character that would be recognised again.

K5.stone_why: Coarser, bolder facets make the display text read strongly as cut stone or an inscription.
K5.carving_why: Facets are larger but still applied as one system and stay crisp; S and 6 become noticeably polygonal yet digits stay clearly distinguishable.
K5.calm_why: More angular energy than K1/K4 but still steady rather than aggressive.
K5.personality_why: Strong, unmistakable chiselled voice while keeping a classical skeleton.

K6.stone_why: Heavy weight plus strong faceting reads as massive, hewn stone block lettering.
K6.carving_why: Faceting is bold and consistent, digits are clear, but the heavy weight makes cuts feel blunter and some counters crowd.
K6.calm_why: Even the regular titles and body text are heavy, so the page feels loud and dense rather than calm.
K6.personality_why: The most forceful and recognisable voice of the set.

K7.stone_why: Strong, coarse facets give a pronounced carved-stone look like K5.
K7.carving_why: Faceting is coherent overall but some curves (S, 6, 5 bowls) turn uneven and slightly lumpy, edging toward processed rather than chiselled.
K7.calm_why: Steady weight, though the irregular angularity adds a touch of restlessness.
K7.personality_why: Distinct hewn character, but the irregularity reads somewhat more processed than designed.
